name: Thematic framing (Bağlamsal çerçeveleme)
definition: The text places an event inside a trend, process or institutional context. This is not a flaw in itself; which context is chosen shapes the reading.
necessary_conditions: An identifiable event is the news.
The outlet's own headline or lede places it in a wider trend, series or institutional context (figures over time, earlier cases, a policy process).
detection_cues: A trend figure alongside the single event.
non_examples: The outlet quotes or attributes the wording to a named speaker and reports it, disputes it or rejects it; the wording is the speaker's, not the outlet's.
An opinion column, interview or signed commentary, where evaluative or argumentative language is the expected form.
Background added by an agency wire that every outlet in the text carries in identical words.
mitigations: None needed; note which context was chosen.
questions: Which context did the outlet choose, and did others choose a different one?
limitations: Metnin ne yaptığını tanımlar; niyet hakkında bir şey söylemez. Describes what the text does and says nothing about purpose. Assessed from headlines and ledes only; not validated against human-reviewed news.
provenance: LAB-ONLY PROPOSAL, not reviewed, not in production. Operationalised from the vendored Mesa spec thematic_framing (definition and annotation boundary) and data/reference/editorial.json.
